fit: strawberries pooled with other fruit in falls-hospitalization cohort
assessment: In 1,429 older women followed for up to 14.5 years, the adjusted HR for other fruit including strawberries was 1.00 (95% CI 0.98 to 1.03) per 20 g/day. No strawberry-specific estimate, Parkinson stratum or recurrent fall count.

fit: randomized six-fruit whole-food crossover and postural sway
assessment: Strawberries were one of six supplied fruits then were among those blended before the final evaluation. In 37 adults with balance measurements, the time-by-phase sway comparison had p=.457. No fall counts or separate strawberry effect.

fit: Parkinson diagnostic strawberry odor in freezing groups
assessment: Nominal strawberry odor item p=.039 in Table 2 for Parkinson freezer versus non-freezer discrimination. Strawberry was not in the final three-item panel. There was no fruit consumption intervention or falls endpoint.

fit: combined dietary produce and retrospective fall injury
assessment: Inadequate combined fruit and vegetable intake had adjusted OR 1.41 (95% CI 1.05 to 1.90) for prior-year fall injury. Cross-sectional design, no fruit-specific effect and no Parkinson stratum.

fit: combined food category and previous-year fall report
assessment: Cross-sectional public-housing study estimates adjusted OR 0.55 (95% CI 0.37 to 0.83) for a prior-year fall with daily fruit and vegetable consumption. No individual fruit or Parkinson comparison.

fit: total fruit frequency and falls with fracture in a case-control study
assessment: Case-control analysis compares aggregate fruit consumption among fracture-associated fall cases and controls. It does not isolate strawberries, recurrent events or Parkinson disease.

fit: strawberry extract feeding and aging mouse motor tests
assessment: The author abstract reports no reversal of aged-mouse rod, wire, plank or screen deficits with strawberry extract. Extract levels and arm-specific estimates require the original report.

fit: strawberry extract versus other feeds in rats
assessment: In the primary article Figure 3 and motor results show that only the blueberry arm improved rod walking and rotarod performance. Strawberry had distinct neurochemical results. Aged rats and extract do not identify raw fruit effects in Parkinson disease.

fit: optional strawberry or blackcurrant jam in a mixed-food endurance study
assessment: Eight participants tested chili versus control pancakes. Jam was optional and not assigned by type. Plank endurance cannot be attributed to strawberry or translated to falls.
Strawberries contribute to modeled dietary contaminant estimates. Residue and dietary modeling are the exposures and no falls or Parkinson endpoint was assessed.

fit: strawberry plant challenge cited in sulfur review
assessment: A plant pathology example explicitly includes strawberry challenged with fungi and reports no observed sulfur accumulation under the tested conditions. This review contains no human ingestion or falls comparison.
The primary horticultural study treats strawberry plants with foliar melatonin under aluminum stress and reports plant performance and fruit quality. No patient or dietary falls outcome is studied.

fit: isolated lupeol in a mouse model
assessment: Strawberry is listed among food sources of lupeol. The mouse intervention uses the isolated compound and has no raw strawberry arm or clinical falls.

fit: leaf extract in Parkinson-related cells and a mouse motor model
assessment: Rotenone-treated mice fed strawberry leaf extract had longer day-28 rotarod latency at high dose and shorter pole T-turn. The report has no edible raw fruit arm or spontaneous Parkinson fall frequency.
